rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `awk 'NR>=104 && NR<=134' <file> | grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*'` → 8 bold spans in chunk 8 (lines 117 'A single orchestrator', 118 'Phase-organised skill catalogue.', 119 'Design principles', 123 'Front-loaded read-only analysis.', 124 'Mandatory gates fire positionally', 125 'Re-invocation as control flow.', 126 'CLAUDE.md as half the system.', 128 'scales cross-repo'; the 'Explicit load. / Orchestrator composition. / CLAUDE.md routing. / Hand-off pipelines.' list at lines 110-113 uses single-asterisk italics, not bold, and doesn't count). Each span is individually inside the ≲5-word handle cap, but 8 on one slide is well past 'a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' — considered that carve-out and reject it: these are ad hoc descriptive labels the author coined for THIS worked example (single orchestrator, phase-organised catalogue, design principles enforced, etc.), not the curriculum's own named laws/governors (e.g. the file's own backing block reserves 'law:' for things like requisite-variety) — a consolidation slide of the training's LAWS is a narrower thing than a slide that labels several of one practitioner's design choices. Also considered and reject the reading-list/lookup-surface waiver (§9): this chunk is a sequential worked-example narrative meant to be read start-to-finish (file's own 'Supplementary meta' note: '15-25 min student read'), not a page a reader consults to find one row answering a question — 'Scope is the surface, not the file type' cuts against extending the lookup-surface waiver to a narrative case-study slide inside a reading-walk supplementary. So the base §9 budget (≤1 on a narrative slide) applies and 8 bolded labels exceeds it. Chunk 9 (`awk 'NR>=135 && NR<=146'` same grep): 3 bold spans, lines 139 'What shape is your real work?' (6 words), 141 'How much orchestration do you want to author?' (8 words), 143 'What review bandwidth do you have?' (6 words) — each bolds the FULL filter question rather than a ≲5-word label, exceeding the handle cap even under the most generous reading-list/menu waiver, which explicitly keeps the handle cap live ('The ≲5-word handle cap is NOT off') and names exactly this failure ('Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover'). Harm: on neither slide does an accept-note cover this; a reader scanning either slide for its one handle finds several full-sentence bolds instead, flattening the bold signal into noise. Standing, non-blocking, unaddressed across multiple prior slides passes on this file.
